title: Pack the Backpack
statement:
A hiker can carry at most `capacity` kilograms. There are several items; item `i` weighs `weights[i]` kilograms and is worth `values[i]`. Each item can be taken **at most once**.

Return the **largest total value** the hiker can carry without going over the weight limit.

examples.explanation: Take the items weighing 3 and 4: value 4 + 5 = 9 (taking 5 + 1 would give only 8).
The only item is too heavy.

hints.nudge: For each item you either take it or leave it. What do you need to know about the leftover capacity?
hints.pattern: Dynamic programming over capacity: best[c] = the best value using weight at most c.
hints.walkthrough: Trying every subset of items takes 2^n time. Let best[c] be the largest value achievable with total weight at most c, using the items processed so far. For a new item (w, v): for each capacity c >= w, you can either ignore the item (best[c]) or take it (best[c - w] + v). Update the capacities from LARGEST to SMALLEST so that best[c - w] still refers to the situation before this item (otherwise the item could be used twice). O(n * capacity) time, O(capacity) space.
